## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building} (`recovery#ff8f0917`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L37))

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I11** Uncached state in a chord oscillator slowed the UI and could crash the unit. Cause: only `0x40000000-0x43ffffff` is cached; mod state beside the effect delay lines (`0x468xxxxx`) was uncached; ~1,000 accesses per block per voice. Fix: copy state to the stack once per block, work there, write it back. Rules: A48.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O16** What section 8 is for: A) the Outbox 8 accessory (dnfw: the image arrived in the DN2 release that added Outbox support; an inference from timing) B) the panel MCU firmware (analog-emu)
- **O14** Analog Rytm MKII CPU: A) rytm-fw-re: MCF5445x (`-mcpu=54455`) B) analog-emu and analog-rytm-mkii-research: MCF5441x (same entry code, CACR/ACR and peripheral blocks as the A4 MKII)

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

## 9. All 43 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] CPU: ColdFire V4e with EMAC, no FPU, on both generations. analog-emu identifies MCF5441x by code and peripheral use. The A4 MK1 mods assemble with `-mcpu=5475 -mno-float`: that is a V4e ISA setting, and with `-mno-float` an FPU instruction becomes an assembly error instead of a crash on the unit. `[hw]` {a4mods} {analog-emu-a4} — `analog-four-keys#e9434b1b` [hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md:13](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md#L13) · Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory
- [hw] MK1: only `0x40000000-0x43ffffff` is cached. ACR0 covers that range and the default is cache-inhibited, so the effect delay lines (`0x468xxxxx` and up) and any mod state placed beside them are uncached: every access is a full bus round trip. An early chord-oscillator build made ~1,000 such accesses per block per voice; the UI slowed and the unit could crash. Copy state to the stack once per block, work there, write it back. `[hw]` {a4mods} ([I11](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i11-uncached-state-in-a-chord-oscillator-slowed-the-ui-and-could-crash-the-unit)) — `analog-four-keys#10b6fafd` [hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md:28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md#L28) · Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory
- [hw] MKII flash part on one unit: Winbond W25Q64 (8 MB, 256-byte pages, 64 KB sectors), reported by the factory console; the Rytm MKII uses an S25FL128S. Compare conflict O8 in [../CONFLICTS.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/CONFLICTS.md). `[hw]` {analog-emu-a4} — `analog-four-keys#c34b64c2` [hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md#L30) · Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory

- [emu] MKII update in the emulator (`[emu]` {analog-emu-a4}): The OS saves its working state to the card, erases 17 x 64 KB from flash `0x80000` and programs the container page by page, then resets. From the first erase to the last page there is no bootable OS in flash; a power cut then needs the DIN recovery. The power-fail handler waits for a running erase. — `analog-four-keys#4a20f839` [hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md:76](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md#L76) · Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / OS update and recovery

- [doc] One interrupt does all digital audio, per 32-sample block (`[doc]` code reading, confirmed by a probe build on a unit) {a4mods}: 1. pick the DMA buffer; 2. run the control block: envelopes, LFOs and per-track levels, which turn each volume into (a) a send gain plus pan and (b) the analog dry VCA words; 3. generate the four digital noise sources; 4. run the FX block: the codec's receive frames (eight slots per sample, six used: four voices and the stereo input) are mixed into three stereo send buses, then chorus, delay and reverb run, and only their summed returns go out to the DAC; 5. send the CV/voice frame to the hardware. — `analog-four-keys#9c6b184b` [hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md:33](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-four-keys.md#L33) · Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Audio engine (MK1 OS 1.55 names; layout the same on 1.56)
